limitations: COLD-inspired stdlib analysis protocol shared by both framework labels, not a neural model or a complete COLD system. Saliency only proposes subsets; selection uses actual comparable host retraining and measurements.

Training-only saliency, feature/source-field lineage and explicitly protected indices/groups are required. All members of every protected group survive; insufficient budgets are rejected. The full baseline and each distinct physical subset must be retrained by the host under the fixed training budget.

Each callback must attest retrained=True and physical_pruning=True, return exact retained_indices and unchanged context, unique train_run_id, implementation_id, finite validation_quality and positive latency_ms. Attestations are not proof: the host retains auditable artifacts and owns the actual GPU trainer.

Context fixes task/dataset/train/validation identity, maximize quality metric, training budget, seed and serving profile (hardware, batch/candidate count, concurrency, latency statistic and feature-lookup inclusion). Model-only latency cannot establish end-to-end savings; multiplying inputs by zero is not physical pruning.

At least one quality floor or maximum absolute baseline quality drop is required. Reports every trial, feasible Pareto candidates and the highest-quality feasible selection (or None). No QPS, acquisition-cost optimization, online-learning implementation or task-effectiveness claim.

output_contract.shape: {context, saliency_split, latency_budget_ms, quality_floor, latency_scope, baseline, trials, pareto_candidates, selected}; selected is None if infeasible

AUC uses original probabilities with half credit for ties and is undefined for a zero-effective-weight class. LogLoss alone uses explicit epsilon clipping; clipping counts and class conditional/contribution losses are reported.

output_contract.shape: {baseline, candidate, delta, comparison, paired_loss_changes, dataset_id, split_id}
